The compatibility hidden in the short proof

The book’s pullback-preservation lemma proves that \(\Fun (T,-)\) preserves pullbacks by testing with \(\Map (S,-)\) and then uncurrying. The corner equivalences are \[ u_Z\colon \Map (S,\Fun (T,Z))\iso \Map (S\times T,Z). \] To use them, we must compare the specified commutativity identifications as well as the four arrows. This note expands that step and explains how the resulting comparison transfers the pullback property.

We work with the absolute categories and the mapping-anima and functor-category structures of Sections 1.1–1.7. The cone conversion below does not require a pullback hypothesis. The later application also uses the pullback structure of Section 1.6. Statements about parameters \(X\) below explicitly require \(X\) to be an anima.

Keeping the commutativity data

For a cospan \(C\xrightarrow {f}E\xleftarrow {g}D\), a cone on \(X\) consists of \(a\colon X\to C\), \(b\colon X\to D\), and an identification \(\theta \colon f\circ a=g\circ b\). A comparison of cones from \((a,b,\theta )\) to \((a',b',\theta ')\) consists of identifications \(\alpha \colon a=a'\) and \(\beta \colon b=b'\), together with an identification \[ \theta '\cdot (f\circ \alpha )=(g\circ \beta )\cdot \theta . \] Here a dot denotes composition of identifications, with the right-hand identification applied first. Thus the comparison remembers a filling of the square between the two matchings. Precomposition of a cone uses the specified associativity identifications to give its new matching. We write \(h^*q\) for this cone and \(q\simeq q'\) for a comparison of cones in this sense.

Fix categories \(S,T\) and put \[ A_Z=\Map (S,\Fun (T,Z)),\qquad B_Z=\Map (S\times T,Z). \] Write \(f_A,g_A\) and \(f_B,g_B\) for the induced postcomposition functors on these two families. These symbols name the cospans used below; we do not need to construct a category of all cones.

Supplementary Lemma 1. For every anima \(X\), there are conversions \(U_X\) and \(V_X\) between cones on \(X\) over \((f_A,g_A)\) and over \((f_B,g_B)\). For a cone \(r=(a,b,\theta )\), the legs of \(U_X(r)\) are \(u_C\circ a\) and \(u_D\circ b\). Both conversions take comparisons of cones to comparisons of cones, and there are comparisons \(V_X(U_X(r))\simeq r\) and \(U_X(V_X(t))\simeq t\). Moreover, a comparison \(U_X(r)\simeq U_X(r')\) gives a comparison \(r\simeq r'\).

Proof idea

Uncurry the legs and matching of \(r\) twice. This gives a cone over \((f,g)\) on \((X\times S)\times T\). Restrict along the associativity equivalence \(X\times (S\times T)\to (X\times S)\times T\), and curry into the mapping anima for \(S\times T\). The resulting legs are identified with \(u_C\circ a\) and \(u_D\circ b\). Transport the matching along these two identifications to obtain exactly these legs.

For the reverse conversion, uncurry a cone over \((f_B,g_B)\), change the parenthesization in the opposite direction, and curry first into the functor category and then into the mapping anima. The evaluation comparisons and the inverse comparisons for product associativity give the two round trips. These are comparisons of whole cones, so they retain compatibility with the matchings. Uncurrying comparisons and reflecting them through the relevant mapping equivalences also gives the final reflection assertion. □

Comparing the specified squares

Let \(q=(p,r,\eta )\) be any cone over \((f,g)\) with vertex \(W\). Denote the cones obtained by the specified postcomposition constructions by \(A(q)\) and \(B(q)\), with vertices \(A_W\) and \(B_W\) respectively.

Supplementary Lemma 2. For every anima \(X\) and every \(h\colon X\to A_W\), there is a comparison \[ U_X\bigl (h^*A(q)\bigr )\simeq (u_W\circ h)^*B(q). \] In particular, converting \(A(q)\) gives a cone comparison with \(u_W^*B(q)\). This assertion does not require \(q\) to be a pullback cone.

Proof idea

Double uncurrying and reassociation turn \(h\) into a functor \(\bar h\colon X\times (S\times T)\to W\). The evaluation comparison for the specified mapped cone identifies the uncurried left-hand cone with \(\bar h^*q\). Uncurrying \(u_W\circ h\) gives a second functor into \(W\), equipped with the comparison expressing that \(u_W\) represents uncurrying. Acting on \(q\) by this comparison compares the two induced cones, including their matching identifications. Reflection through the mapping equivalence gives the asserted cone comparison.

More explicitly, let \(\alpha \) and \(\beta \) be its two leg comparisons and let \(\mu \) and \(\nu \) be the source and target matchings. The compatibility supplied by the comparison is \[ \nu \cdot (f_B\circ \alpha )=(g_B\circ \beta )\cdot \mu . \] Equivalently, after transporting \(\mu \) along \(\alpha \) and \(\beta \), it is identified with \(\nu \). This is the precise matching obligation. Taking \(X=A_W\) and \(h\) the identity, and inserting the unit comparisons, gives the assertion about the square itself. The category \(A_W\) is an anima. □

The leg comparisons here are those constructed by this cone conversion. The argument does not require an additional identification with independently chosen postcomposition-naturality witnesses. Nor does it assert all higher coherence laws for a category of cone diagrams.

Transferring the pullback property

Supplementary Lemma 3. Let \(s\) and \(t\) be cones over two cospans, with vertices \(Y\) and \(Z\), and let \(u\colon Y\to Z\) be an equivalence. Suppose that, for every anima \(X\), a conversion \(K_X\) between cones over the two cospans preserves and reflects cone comparisons, and is equipped, for every \(h\colon X\to Y\), with a comparison \[ K_X(h^*s)\simeq (u\circ h)^*t. \] If \(t\) is a pullback cone, \(Y\) is an anima, and the chosen pullback of the source cospan is an anima, then \(s\) is a pullback cone.

Proof idea

For a cone \(r\) on an anima \(X\) over the source cospan, factor \(K_X(r)\) through \(t\). Lift the factorizing functor through \(u\). The displayed comparison and reflection of cone comparisons identify the cone induced by this lift with \(r\).

If two functors \(h,k\colon X\to Y\) induce comparable cones, applying \(K_X\) and the displayed comparisons gives comparable cones induced by \(u\circ h\) and \(u\circ k\). The pullback property of \(t\) gives an identification between these functors, which reflects through \(u\).

Apply the first construction to the chosen pullback cone of the source cospan. It supplies a candidate inverse to the comparison from \(Y\) to that pullback. Its first inverse comparison follows from its cone computation and the universal property of the chosen pullback. The second follows from the reflection property just proved, applied with \(X=Y\). These two tests are legitimate by the anima hypotheses and prove that the comparison is an equivalence. □

Supplementary Corollary 4. For every category \(T\), postcomposition sends a pullback cone \(q\) to a pullback cone under \(\Fun (T,-)\), with its specified commutativity identification.

Proof idea

For every category \(S\), the cone \(B(q)\) is a pullback by the mapping-anima criterion in Section 1.6. Apply Supplementary Lemma 3 using \(u_W\), the conversion of Supplementary Lemma 1, and the comparison of Supplementary Lemma 2. Its anima hypotheses hold: \(A_W\) is a mapping anima, and pullbacks of animae are animae. Thus \(A(q)\) is a pullback for every \(S\). Mapping-anima detection now shows that the specified \(\Fun (T,-)\) cone is a pullback. This recovers the short argument in the book with its compatibility step made explicit. □
